name: Nesa
rootCause: Cosmos EVM's StateDB tracked only an account's spendable balance, while x/staking and the staking precompile let a vesting account delegate locked coins. Delegating more than the spendable balance made the write-back in StateDB.SubBalance underflow (unchecked uint256) to ~2^256. The fix had been on main since May but shipped in v0.6.2 / v0.7.2 only on 19 Aug; the chain was still on an unpatched version. On Nesa the attacker inflated a ~1.1M NES deposit and withdrew 257.7M NES (~25.8% of supply) to Ethereum via Hyperlane; thin liquidity limited net profit to roughly $60K-240K, so the nominal loss overstates what was realised.

Delegating more than the spendable balance made the write-back in StateDB.SubBalance underflow (unchecked uint256) to ~2^256. The fix had been on main since May but shipped in v0.6.2 / v0.7.2 only on 19 Aug; the chain was still on an unpatched version. An attacker bridged 257.7 million NES, roughly $50 million, from Nesa to Ethereum in an incident consistent with the Cosmos EVM bug chain that hit MANTRA, TAC, and KiiChain. Nesa never published the mechanism; Bubblemaps estimated slippage cut net profit to roughly $60k.

Nesa Chain disclosed malicious activity on 2026-08-24 tied to a vulnerability in the shared Cosmos EVM module used by several Cosmos SDK networks. Public reporting stated that an attacker inflated NES balances on Nesa, bridged manipulated tokens to Ethereum, and attempted to liquidate them through decentralized exchanges, although realized proceeds were reportedly far smaller than the nominal inflated value. Public reporting consistently attributed the incident to a balance-accounting vulnerability in the shared Cosmos EVM module used by Nesa and other Cosmos SDK chains.
